assertions.name: every_corpus_letter_has_negative_alternating_character
assertions.source: sigma -0.900918283956, bar-fixed -1.00544843335, sigma^-1 -1.10997858275 -- all three strictly negative at the proton pin. This is the whole mechanism: the sign of a product of them depends on nothing but how many there are. Lean: AltCharShiftMultiset.letterChar_neg

assertions.name: no_corpus_letter_is_anywhere_near_the_positivity_threshold
assertions.source: a letter needs shift d >= 1/(q^2-1) = 4.30937049811 to reach non-negative character. The largest corpus shift is 0.0, short by 4.30937049811. This is the honest limit of the exclusion: it covers the corpus alphabet, not every conceivable alphabet

assertions.name: the_sign_is_length_parity_on_all_1092_words_exhaustively
assertions.source: all 1092 words over the 3-letter alphabet at lengths 1..6 have sign exactly (-1)^length -- 0 exceptions. Exhaustive, not sampled: 3+9+27+81+243+729. Generators were varied along each word too, confirming the generator-blindness altChar_regen states

assertions.name: the_engine_route_agrees_and_shows_the_same_parity
assertions.source: multiplying the Hoefsmit (1,1,1) generator matrices and taking the trace reproduces the per-letter product to 2.28441e-39 across lengths 1..6, and carries the same sign parity. The scalar model is not assumed -- it is confirmed against the engine

assertions.name: both_corpus_nucleon_words_are_odd_length_and_negative
assertions.source: both are 11 letters (ODD) and both have strictly negative alternating character -- p -0.73922357077, n -0.91076221455. The (1,1,1) block is 1-dimensional, so PSD there is 0 <= character: under scope (B) both are excluded, and by the parity theorem so is EVERY 11-letter word over this alphabet, whatever its letters. Lean: no_eleven_letter_word_is_alt_psd

assertions.name: even_length_words_are_positive_so_the_parity_discriminates
assertions.source: the 6-letter gamma-gamma core has character 1.0 (exactly 1, as altChar_eq_one requires) and the 2-letter gluon pair 0.811653754366 -- both POSITIVE. So the result is not 'the character is always negative'; it is a parity. This is also the consistency check against altChar_eq_one, which pins every gamma-gamma word at 1: gamma-gamma words have EVEN length

description: The alternating character's SIGN is (-1)^length over the corpus alphabet: every letter has strictly negative character (-1/q, -(q^2+1)/(2q), -q), so a product of them is decided in sign by nothing but how many there are. Proved first in Lean (QOU.Mass.AltCharShiftMultiset.wordChar_sign, sorry-free); this probe confirms it exhaustively over all 3^n words for n = 1..6 and by an INDEPENDENT engine route (Hoefsmit (1,1,1) matrices). CONSEQUENCE: under the owner-selected SDP scope (B) whole element, the alternating block is 1-dimensional so PSD there is 0 <= character; the nucleon budget is 11, which is ODD; so the entire 11-crossing construction is excluded, not merely a choice of letters within it. This REFRAMES bean qou-99qc item 2: no principle for the 5 un-ruled letters can repair an obstruction that does not depend on them.

positivity_threshold.meaning: a letter would need this shift to reach non-negative character; no corpus letter is close, so the exclusion covers the corpus alphabet and not every alphabet

exhaustive_parity.method: all 3^n words over the 3-letter alphabet, n = 1..6, with generators varied along each word

consequence_under_scope_B.scope: (B) whole element -- owner ruling 2026-09-13, bean qou-99qc
consequence_under_scope_B.verdict: every 11-letter word over the corpus alphabet is excluded, independent of which letters carry the p/n asymmetry
consequence_under_scope_B.reframes: bean qou-99qc item 2 asked for a principle for the 5 un-ruled letters that is bar-consistent AND whole-element PSD-admissible. No such principle exists at length 11: the obstruction does not depend on those letters
consequence_under_scope_B.second_independent_obstruction: gamma-gamma words have even length (gammaGamma_length_even), which is why the construction half reaches only 6 of 11. The SDP half demands even length too, by a different argument

scope.invariant: the sign of the alternating character, = (-1)^length
scope.honest_limit: per-letter negativity fails for a letter with shift d >= 1/(q^2-1) ~ 4.31; every corpus letter is in {0, -1/2, -1}
scope.what_is_NOT_claimed: that no nucleon word exists -- only that none of ODD length over this alphabet is admissible in the alternating block under scope (B)
